text:
sara: pushed a profiling run mixing short chat prompts and long-context streams. results attached in thread, tl;dr some unexpected p99 regressions on the 'fast' decode-path.
max: saw ~11% p99 increase on the same machines, repro via perf-dashboard link -> https://perf.redwood/reports/177900 | logs show more context-switches in the batcher.
dani: looked at the flamegraphs — kernel selection is oscillating between fp16-optimal and the int8-emulated path during sustained traffic. that thrash looks correlated with decode-rate changes.
kevin: also noticed kv cache churn. when KV hit-rate dips below ~75% we see more KV prefetch + eviction which inflates decode time. probably due to token_budget being too small for long-context cohorts.
sara: exact config used for the run:
```
batcher.config:
{
  "queue_policy": "cohort_prefer",
  "cohort_keys": ["len_bin","decode_tier"],
  "token_budget_target": 1536,
  "len_bins": [0,64,256,1024],
  "decode_tiers": ["fast","med","slow"]
}
```
max: fwiw, the classifier that assigns decode_tier is based on first-50-token decode slope (tokens/sec). thresholds: fast>120t/s, med 40-120, slow<40.
dani: hypothesis: batching by len_bin only is mixing high-decode-rate short prompts with slow streaming ones and the kernel selector flips to the slower kernel for the whole batch. need a stricter cohorting rule or pre-batch split.
kevin: there9s also a KV budget angle — small token_budget_target forces aggressive KV eviction to free slots for new prefixes, which hurts long-context reuses. increasing token_budget for len>256 reduced eviction in earlier microbench.
ops-bot: profile-run #1779001234 completed: p95=84ms p99=312ms throughput=1.2k rps. artifacts: gs://redwood-profiles/1779001234.tar.gz
dani: quick snip from logs showing kernel swap noise: 
```
[2026-03-14T10:12:04Z] kernel: select fp16-optimal for model A seq=64
[2026-03-14T10:12:05Z] kernel: select int8-emulated for model A seq=256
[2026-03-14T10:12:05Z] kernel: select fp16-optimal for model A seq=64
[2026-03-14T10:12:06Z] decode: batch latency jump +42ms
```
sara: proposed next experiments: 1) cohort by decode_tier first, len_bin second (so fast-only batches form quickly), 2) raise token_budget_target to 4096 for len_bin>=256, 3) force kernel-stable hint: prefer fp16 when mixed but slow decode_tier present to avoid thrash.
max: add metric to track "kernel-flips-per-minute" and correlate with p99, should be a good signal.
kevin: I'll run an A/B on two fleet slices: slice A uses current config, slice B uses sara's config with token_budget bump and cohorting change. run for 30m at 100% traffic replay.
sara: also watch KV-hit-rate, add alert if it drops >10% vs baseline (so we catch prefetch thrash early).
deploy-bot: perf-regression alert: +9.8% p99 on fleet slice 42 (g4dn-xlarge), triggered at 1779001789.
dani: if the kernel hint approach works, we might accept slightly higher median for much lower p99. tradeoff is fine for many product routes.
kevin: experiment scheduled, I'll post results in this thread. thanks! :thumbsup:
sara: action items summarized: (sara) run cohort-first decode_tier experiments; (kevin) A/B rollout; (dani) add kernel-flip metric and dashboard; (max) add KV-hit alert. will reconvene after runs (~2h).
kevin: noted, starting replay now.
ops-bot: experiment B live at 1779002001, routing 100% replay to slice B.
